solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Chill out? Do this to maintain warmth? (4,4,5,2)

blocks.note: calm down, stop losing your temper: an idiom, not a temperature
taken literally: stay dressed and you stay warm

annotation.surface: Advice to someone overheating, which turns into practical advice about staying warm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chill' tempts you towards cold, but the first half is the idiom for calming down; the second reads the same phrase literally, where keeping clothes on keeps you warm.
annotation.definitionFit: To keep your shirt on is to stay calm, and a shirt left on keeps the heat in.

entries.clue: One skewered king on its file with bishop by a bishop (5)

blocks.note: K is the chess symbol for king
a chess king starts on the e-file
B is the chess symbol for bishop
used as printed
B again, the second bishop

annotation.surface: A chess position where the king is pinned on its file by a pair of bishops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skewered' is a real chess term for an attack through one piece to another, so the whole clue reads as chess; in fact it defines food on a skewer.
annotation.definitionFit: A kebab is pieces of meat threaded on a skewer, so it is one skewered.

entries.clue: Food parcels broken into by soldiers? (9)

annotation.definition: Food parcels broken into by soldiers?

blocks.note: the surface offers aid packages; read literally, anything wrapped around food
not looted by troops: soldiers are fingers of toast, dipped into a boiled egg through its top

annotation.surface: Relief supplies being looted by troops.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain, soldiers are thin fingers of toast for dipping into a soft-boiled egg, so the parcels are eggs in their shells.
annotation.definitionFit: An eggshell wraps the food inside, and the toast soldiers break through it.

entries.clue: Beastly type kidnaps North American (4)

indicatorNotes.kidnaps: to kidnap is to take and hold someone, so YAK holds N inside it

blocks.note: a yak is a type of beast, the Tibetan ox
N is the compass abbreviation

annotation.surface: A monster abducting a man from the States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'North American' reads as one phrase, but North is split off to give N, leaving American as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal, originally British, nickname for someone from the United States.

entries.clue: A French editor with trapped wind’s stuffy (7)

indicatorNotes.with trapped: UN and ED hold AIR trapped between them

blocks.note: un is French for a
air in motion is wind
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

annotation.surface: A French newspaper editor suffering from indigestion.
annotation.walkthrough: The trapped wind sounds like a digestive complaint; it is just a gust of the stuff that fills rooms. The definition sits at the end after the 's.
annotation.definitionFit: A room nobody has aired keeps its stale air, which is what stuffy describes.

entries.clue: I’m into quotes about Hebrew, say (7)

indicatorNotes.into: into means entering, so I'M goes inside the letters of CITES
indicatorNotes.about: about means turned round, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: to quote is to cite
used as printed

annotation.surface: Someone who enjoys quoting a Hebrew text.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quotes' looks like a noun, quotations; it is a verb. 'About' governs everything before it, so the insertion happens first and the reversal last.
annotation.definitionFit: Hebrew is one of the Semitic languages, hence the 'say'.

entries.clue: Consumption sadly isn’t gone, I admitted (9)

indicatorNotes.sadly: sadly means badly, so the letters come out in a poor order
indicatorNotes.admitted: the letters let I in, like a club admitting a guest

blocks.note: the letters of ISNT GONE rearranged
used as printed, slipped in between INGEST and ON

annotation.surface: A lament that the illness called consumption hasn't gone away.
annotation.walkthrough: Consumption was the old name for tuberculosis, which suits 'sadly isn't gone', but here it just means eating.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean the act of eating or swallowing.

entries.clue: State of heavyweight? God-awful primarily! (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first, so take the first letters of God-awful

blocks.note: a ton is a heavy weight
the first letters of God and awful

annotation.surface: A boxer's reaction to the dreadful condition of a heavyweight fighter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State of heavyweight' reads as a condition; State is actually the definition, a nation.
annotation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom, a sovereign state.

entries.clue: New heed given to object in close encounter? (4,5)

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
to give ear is to pay heed
an object is a thing

annotation.surface: Fresh attention paid to a UFO sighting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close encounter' calls up aliens, which is why an object turns up; it just means a narrow escape.
annotation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, a close shave.

entries.clue: One will leave and go away briefly near Iowa (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: briefly means cut short, so BEGONE loses its last letter

blocks.note: begone = go away, minus its final E
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

annotation.surface: Someone in the Midwest announcing they are off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One will leave' sounds like a person departing; it is a plant that will put out leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: A begonia is a flowering plant, and plants leave in the sense of producing leaves.

entries.clue: Trump slogan appearing around NHS unit makes you colour (7)

indicatorNotes.appearing around: MAGA sits around ENT, splitting into MAG and A

blocks.note: Make America Great Again
Ear, Nose and Throat, a hospital department; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service

annotation.surface: A political slogan plastered around a hospital ward, which is enough to make you blush.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Makes you colour' reads as makes you blush; colour is just the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific colour named for its hue, a purplish red, so colour is the broad class.

entries.clue: Arty type’s shocking utterance about heroin (4)

indicatorNotes.about: BOO goes about H, surrounding it

blocks.note: boo! is shouted to give someone a fright
H is slang for heroin

annotation.surface: A bohemian artist saying something outrageous about drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: The shocking utterance sounds like a scandalous remark, but it is the word you shout to make someone jump.
annotation.definitionFit: A boho is a bohemian, an unconventional artistic type.

entries.clue: I’m against going for assessment with social worker (10)

blocks.note: pro = for, in favour of
a test is an assessment
ants are social insects, and the worker is a caste of ant

annotation.surface: Someone objecting to being assessed with a social worker present.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: a protestant is literally one who protests, so 'I'm against'. The social worker is an insect, not a council employee.
annotation.definitionFit: A protestant, in the literal sense, is one who protests, one who is against something.

entries.clue: Everything occupies mostly irritable dabbler (7)

indicatorNotes.occupies: ALL occupies MARD, sitting inside it
indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means all but the last letter, so MARDY drops its Y

blocks.note: mardy is northern English for sulky or irritable, cut short
all = everything

annotation.surface: An amateur who is grumpy most of the time.
annotation.walkthrough: A dabbler looks like an amateur, but a mallard is a dabbling duck, feeding at the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: The mallard is a dabbling duck, one that dabbles at the surface for food.

entries.clue: Sad case Mr Wrong walked all over (9)

indicatorNotes.Wrong: the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters of SAD CASE MR rearranged

annotation.surface: A pitiful man, the wrong partner, who treated someone as a doormat.
annotation.walkthrough: Mr Wrong reads as a bad boyfriend, but Wrong is the anagram indicator and Mr is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To massacre a side in a game is to beat it overwhelmingly, to walk all over it.

entries.clue: Republican to probe if Apollo cooked up hoax (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to probe: R goes into the other letters, as a probe does
indicatorNotes.cooked up: cooked up means invented, the letters remade

blocks.note: the letters of IF APOLLO rearranged
R is the abbreviation for Republican, placed after AP

annotation.surface: A conspiracy theorist wanting to investigate whether the Moon landings were faked.
annotation.walkthrough: The Apollo Moon-landing hoax is a real conspiracy theory, which is why 'hoax' feels like part of the story rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by custom: the trick played on the first of April names any such prank.

entries.clue: Red slogan repeated by one around lunchtime (7)

indicatorNotes.around: CHANT goes around I, holding it

blocks.note: a chant is a slogan repeated over and over
one o'clock, written as the Roman numeral I
one is I in Roman numerals, placed beside

annotation.surface: A communist slogan chanted by someone at midday.
annotation.walkthrough: Red suggests communism beside a slogan, but it is the definition, a wine. Lunchtime is one o'clock, so it gives I.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: red stands for red wine, and this Tuscan wine is one.

entries.clue: Those giving cronies jobs in new stone pits (9)

indicatorNotes.new: the letters are given a new order

blocks.note: the letters of STONE PITS rearranged

annotation.surface: Bosses handing out jobs to pals in a fresh quarry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New' reads as describing the pits, but it tells you to remake their letters; 'in' just joins the halves.
annotation.definitionFit: Nepotists favour friends and relatives when giving out posts.

entries.clue: Music producer Oasis trumpeted for a while (7)
Old picture taken by police of the forehead (7)

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
O is the abbreviation for old
pic is short for picture

annotation.surface: A mugshot taken by the police, perhaps just of the head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken by police' tempts you to think of a mugshot, but it just places the police letters first.
annotation.definitionFit: Metopic is the anatomical adjective for the forehead, as in the metopic suture.

entries.clue: Bit of a lad some might have for dinner? (4,3)

annotation.definition: Bit of a lad some might have for dinner?

blocks.note: the idiom means a rogue; read literally, a piece of a young man
the 'some' are cannibals, and the answer is their supposed name for the meat

annotation.surface: A cheeky young man invited round for a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a lad' is the idiom for a rogue, but here it is literally a piece of a person, and the 'some' are cannibals.
annotation.definitionFit: Long pig is said to be the cannibal's term for human flesh, so a bit of a lad on the plate.

entries.clue: Academic was first to secure merit (7)

indicatorNotes.secure: LED holds EARN securely inside it

blocks.note: to lead is to be first
to merit is to earn

annotation.surface: A scholar who got in first to win an award.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Secure' looks like the verb win, as in secure a prize; here it means hold fast, the containment signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) means scholarly, academic.

entries.clue: A tall hat worn around North Dakota etc. (3,3,4)

indicatorNotes.worn: worn means battered out of shape, so the letters change order
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around ND

blocks.note: the letters of A TALL HAT rearranged
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota, set after the first A

annotation.surface: Someone in North Dakota sporting a tall hat, a cowboy hat perhaps.
annotation.walkthrough: The hat is worn on the head, but 'worn' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: 'And all that' ends a list the way etc. does.

entries.clue: Artist, say, in German article (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the letters for 'say' sit inside the article

blocks.note: das is the German neuter 'the'
e.g. = for example, say

annotation.surface: A painter mentioned in a German magazine piece.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'Artist' from 'say'; say gives EG, and the article is a grammatical one, not a feature piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter.

entries.clue: Animal flatulence flipping overwhelms vet ultimately (4)

indicatorNotes.flipping: to flip something is to turn it over, so the assembled letters are read backwards
indicatorNotes.overwhelms: GAS overwhelms T, closing over it
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means last, so the final letter of vet

blocks.note: flatulence is wind, gas
the last letter of vet

annotation.surface: A farmyard creature with such awful wind that it floors the vet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild swear word; it is the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the male deer is one kind of animal.

entries.clue: Unripe lime? (5)

blocks.note: fruit not yet ready to eat, named by its colour
lime is a colour as well as a fruit; the ? marks a definition by example

annotation.surface: A question about a lime that is not ready yet.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words look like one fruit, but each defines the answer: lime is a colour as well as a fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the colour describes fruit before it ripens, and lime is an example of that colour.

entries.clue: A few throwing out old piece of Ercol? Duck! (4)

indicatorNotes.throwing out: to throw out is to discard, so the letter for old is removed from the word
indicatorNotes.piece of: a piece of Ercol is just its first letter

blocks.note: some = a few, minus O for old
the first letter of Ercol, a British furniture maker

annotation.surface: Someone chucking out old Ercol furniture, followed by a warning to dodge a flying chair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck!' reads as a shout to get down; it is the definition, a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Smee is an old name for a duck, especially the smew or wigeon.

entries.clue: After dismissing core members, reggae band get back together (7)

indicatorNotes.After dismissing core members: the core of REGGAE, its middle EGGA, is dismissed, leaving RE

blocks.note: REGGAE without its middle letters EGGA
a band is a musical group

annotation.surface: A reggae band that sacked its key members and then reunites.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Core members' sounds like the heart of the band, but it is the core letters of reggae.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: re- plus group, to form a group again after scattering.

entries.clue: Indian greeting star outside a vacant set (7)

indicatorNotes.outside: outside means on the outer side, so the star's letters wrap around the rest
indicatorNotes.vacant: vacant means emptied, so set keeps only its outer letters S and T

blocks.note: a big name is a star
used as printed
set emptied of its middle E

annotation.surface: A film star greeting people in India on an empty set.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests something celestial or a celebrity by name; a star is a big name, and that word is what wraps around.
annotation.definitionFit: Namaste is the Indian greeting, said with palms pressed together.

entries.clue: Refugee old prince passed by a circuitous route (9,6)

indicatorNotes.by a circuitous route: the letters take a winding path to their places

blocks.note: the letters of OLD PRINCE PASSED rearranged

annotation.surface: An exiled old prince who fled by a roundabout path.
annotation.walkthrough: The prince passing sounds like a death; 'passed' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A displaced person is someone forced from home, a refugee.
